config.scope: Small supervised fixed-horizon two-block dynamics heads on frozen pretrained latent predictions; not a new pretrained world model or validated 3D fracture model.
protocol: Version 2 corrects a pre-impulse position causality defect in version 1. The first target position excludes the future-action input by architecture; subsequent positions may depend on it.

Version 1 is preserved as a diagnostic, not a physically causal world-model result. Version 2 uses a new split seed and distinct history values, without tuning hyperparameters on version-1 test outcomes.
History groups are disjoint across train/validation/test, including paired probe protocols and all future-action variants.
All histories are produced by full valid prescribed loading/unloading. Hidden state is never a prediction input.
Stationary histories share exactly the same observed noisy prefix, preserving the identifiability negative control.
Numeric actions are velocity increments in m/s; event times, camera, material and geometry are fixed and known.
RGB-D features include only prefix part summaries and fixed-prior prefix residuals; V-JEPA features use only prefix input.
PCA and normalization fit on training inputs only. Epoch selection uses validation labels only.
Test interpolation holds out action magnitudes within the training range; extrapolation to 0.42 m/s is reported separately.
Projection minimizes predicted-gap discrepancy within the prefix-RGB-D accepted physics candidates. An empty set remains a failure.
All physical candidate trajectories are shared among methods; no acceleration, uncertainty calibration, novelty or real-world accuracy claim.

features.input: observed four-frame RGB prefix and its foreground mask only

limitations: One known material, camera, geometry and prescribed 1D interface; 44 synthetic history groups only.
Small supervised fixed-horizon heads, not an independently pretrained general world model.
Numeric actions are prescribed velocity increments, not simulated impactor contact or language actions.
All baseline and projection methods share the physical bank; projection adds no simulator speed benefit here.
PCA/normalization use training inputs, epochs use validation responses. No hyperparameter tuning on test results.
Stationary prefixes are identical across histories and cannot uniquely identify damage.
Raw learned gaps/failure scores do not guarantee contact feasibility, damage irreversibility or calibrated probabilities.
Three training seeds quantify optimization variation, not a statistical confidence interval or broad generalization.
Conventional frozen-feature heads, supervised dynamics and candidate projection are not claimed as novel.
